targetText: The history of all countries shows that the working class, exclusively by its own effort, is able to develop only trade union consciousness
summary: Lenin points out that spontaneous worker struggles naturally limit themselves to immediate workplace demands (trade unionism) unless connected to socialist theory.
context: Lenin argues that political class consciousness does not emerge automatically from wage disputes alone; it requires education and broader political analysis.

targetText: quite independently of whether he who belittles that role desires it or not, a strengthening of the influence of bourgeois ideology upon the workers.
summary: Downplaying conscious socialist theory does not make the labour movement neutral; it hands the field to bourgeois ideology.
explanation: Lenin argues there is no middle path between bourgeois and socialist ideology. A movement that relies only on spontaneous trade union struggle will be shaped by the dominant ideas of capitalist society, so conscious theory is a political necessity.
context: This is the foundation of the argument that socialist consciousness must be brought to workers from outside the narrow economic struggle through a political party.

targetText: This is precisely the trend of unbounded opportunism, which passively adapts itself to spontaneity.
summary: Tailing the spontaneous movement and rejecting a plan is opportunism, not respect for the masses.
explanation: Lenin turns the Economists' appeal to the 'masses' against them. By refusing to lead and only reacting to whatever struggle happens to be under way, they passively adapt to existing conditions and abandon the revolutionary aims of the movement.
context: The same criticism was later applied to every current that treated reform of capitalism as the entire programme.
